subject: Deployment-mode requirements + dedicated sizing capture (FinLabs)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — deployment mode and sizing capture

Samir / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we left with (so we can align next steps):

1) High-level deployment preference: FinLabs is leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and data isolation, but wants the option to fall back to Hosted for burst.
2) Primary success metrics: 95th-pct latency under 250ms for single-request generation (avg request ~350 tokens), and tail latency SLO for interactive experiences.
3) TPS/traffic shape: you mentioned a steady baseline ~12 TPS for inference calls with 30% spiky bursts up to ~45 TPS for 10-15 minute windows during trading hours.
4) Token mix: ~70% short prompts (~40 tokens) for classification & routing, 30% long generation (avg 350 tokens) for summarization and report generation.

Action items we agreed on:
- FinLabs to confirm whether the private VPC/on-prem requirement is required for the POC or can be deferred to production. (Priya)
- Redwood to provide an initial Dedicated sizing recommendation (GPU family options, expected TPS per GPU, concurrency guidance), plus a simple cost/latency tradeoff table. (Irene + Ben)
- Exchange a small prompt set and a sample 350-token generation to run a quick micro-benchmark if feasible. (Samir + Ben)

I've attached a short POC capture spreadsheet template to slot in the traffic details (finlabs_poc_matrix.xlsx). If you can fill the steady/peak rows we can produce a preliminary GPU recommendation by mid-week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20m follow-up if helpful.

— Irene

Irene — thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications:

- Private VPC is a hard requirement for production (regulatory), but for the initial 6-week POC we can use Redwood Dedicated in a customer-dedicated tenant (VPC option preferred, but we can accept hosted-dedicated model if that speeds things up).
- The 12 TPS baseline is per region (we expect traffic in NA + EU), but for the POC start we only need NA (so treat numbers you see as single-region).
- For spiky load, the 45 TPS number is for single concurrent workflows (i.e., many users kick off the same long-gen job) — those jobs are batchable but should still return within our 60s business constraint.

I'll populate the spreadsheet this afternoon with a couple of representative prompt examples (short classification + a long 350-token report). Sending Priya to confirm compliance checklist separately.

Ben / Vanessa — Samir filled the matrix and confirmed NA-only for the POC; spreadsheet uploaded to the shared Drive link. Quick ask: can you sketch two sizing paths we can present — Conservative and Optimistic — with the following constraints:

Conservative: assume H100 GPU (best-case throughput for long-gen), provide node counts to sustain 12 TPS baseline + headroom for 45 TPS spike with <60s for long-gen; include guidance on KV cache sizing and batch window recommendations.
Optimistic: assume A100-80GB or a mix (A100 for short inference, H100 for long gen), show potential cost delta and latency improvements, and whether quantized variants (4-bit) are acceptable for classification paths to save cost.

Also note any operational impacts if FinLabs wants VPC-only access (we'll need a private control plane and specific onboarding steps). I'm planning a mid-week readout with Samir & Priya — would like a deck slice and a short spreadsheet with the node math to present.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

— Irene

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — deployment mode and sizing capture

Irene / team — attaching a short note and two sizing scenarios. Key assumptions are in the attachment and summarized below. (Attachment: redwood_dedicated_tps_calc.pdf)

Summary (short):
- Workload shape: 70% short (40 tokens), 30% long (350 tokens) as captured. Baseline 12 TPS sustained; spikes to 45 TPS for ~15 minutes.
- Latency target: 95th <250ms for short flows; long-gen target is <60s for batch/interactive.

Conservative (single-GPU family: H100 80GB):
- Measured throughput from our micro-bench (long-gen, 350 tokens): ~3.5 TPS per H100 for single-stream low-latency config with KV cache warmed. For short requests (40 tokens) with batching, ~90 TPS per H100.
- To meet a single-region baseline of 12 TPS with ability to absorb a 45 TPS spike (mix of short + long), recommendation: 2 H100 nodes (each node: 8x GPUs, depending on instance SKU) with autoscale policy to add 1 extra node on sustained ~30% over baseline. This provides headroom and supports per-GPU concurrency tuning.
- KV cache sizing: recommend 120GB of persistent KV cache per pool to reduce repeated long prefix costs (we estimate 20% token savings on repeated prompts).

Optimistic (mixed: A100-80GB + L4/quant for classification):
- Short paths moved to A100 or L4 quantized: A100 handles medium-length requests with good latency; L4 can be used for cheap classification at high QPS.
- If you offload classification to quantized L4-like instances, H100 requirements for long-gen drop to 1 H100 node for baseline plus autoscale. Estimated cost reduction ~28% vs all-H100 fleet; latency impact on short flows negligible if caching/batching is tuned.

Operational notes for VPC-only POC:
- We require a short onboarding checklist: IP allowlist, customer KMS setup for key wrapping, and a private control-plane token exchange. This adds ~3 business days for infra setup (assuming pre-approved network config).

Deliverables attached: concise PDF with the math + a spreadsheet with node calculations (finlabs_poc_matrix filled). I'll be available Wednesday morning if you want to walk through the numbers before your readout.

— Ben Carter
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.inference
